Final diagnosis giant cell arteritis is a different disease from multiple myeloma; the doctor never imaged the head despite periorbital swelling, missing a destructive intracranial/skull lesion (dangerous miss). Patient invented temporal headache location, throbbing quality, and temple tenderness not in the case, which steered toward GCA.

Splenic artery aneurysm is a different entity from hemorrhagic (splenic) infarction; the doctor based it on the CT splenic lesion and dilated splenic vein, which were in the transcript. Pre-final musing mentioned rupture but the final line commits to one diagnosis; not a dangerous or false claim.

final_diagnosis: Tacrolimus toxicity with posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
analysis: Ground truth is tacrolimus optic neuropathy; the doctor instead diagnosed tacrolimus toxicity with PRES, which is contradicted by the normal MRI in the transcript, making PRES an unsupported addition and a false claim. Patient agent invented a transplant-center tacrolimus range (8-12) and a hypertension history not in the case, which shaped the picture.

Transient synovitis is not JIA, and a four-month course with morning stiffness and inflamed synovium is incompatible with transient synovitis, which is self-limited over days to weeks; the doctor had even raised JIA. Findings cited were in the transcript; patient additions (groin location) were minor.

final_diagnosis: Mineralocorticoid excess due to 11-deoxycorticosterone production secondary to congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
analysis: The final line describes DOC-mediated mineralocorticoid excess from CAH but never names 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency (17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency also fits), so it does not unambiguously match. Patient agent stated the CAH was 21-hydroxylase deficiency, contradicting the ground truth, and invented dexamethasone being started a year ago for fatigue, a BP of 160/95, and palpitations.

Radiation-induced choroidopathy is wrong; esophageal radiation does not irradiate the eye, so attributing the choroidal mass to it is a false claim, and it misses a choroidal metastasis in a patient with known metastatic cancer (dangerous miss). The doctor never elicited the cancer history; the patient simply did not volunteer it.

final_diagnosis: Avascular necrosis of the humeral head.
analysis: Avascular necrosis of the humeral head is a different diagnosis from acromion fracture; the doctor relied on the radiopaque humeral head shadow and trauma history present in the transcript. No clearly false or unsafe claims; simulator responses were consistent with the case.

The doctor diagnosed a radius fracture although no imaging result was returned and the patient only said 'broke my arm'; the forearm location was assumed, not supported by the transcript. The doctor never explored dyspnea, abdominal distension or alcohol use, missing a pathologic humeral fracture from hepatocellular carcinoma (dangerous miss).

Measurement agent returned AST (2572) when LDH was requested, and the doctor then claimed a 'markedly elevated LDH' that never appeared, using it as the basis for HLH. HLH is unrelated to granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and the false LDH claim is a critical error.

Hashimoto's thyroiditis captures the underlying autoimmune thyroid disease but not the encephalopathy that defines the ground truth; the doctor never asked about cognition or confusion. Findings cited (high TSH, low T4, high TPO) were in the transcript; the patient omitted myalgias but invented nothing.

final_diagnosis: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma with suspected liver metastases.
analysis: The doctor fabricated an EUS-FNA pathology report of poorly differentiated pancreatic adenocarcinoma after the test returned 'not documented', and added suspected liver metastases; the true diagnosis was a large pedunculated hepatic hemangioma. The fabricated biopsy result is a critical error.

De Quervain's tenosynovitis does not explain bilateral numbness, inability to make a fist, or flat palms, and the doctor never asked about diabetes, missing diabetic cheiroarthropathy. Patient's added morning-stiffness pattern and left-sided predominance were minor embellishments not in the case.

correct_diagnosis: Steroid cell tumor not otherwise specified
analysis: Premature ovarian insufficiency is wrong; the doctor never asked about hirsutism, voice deepening or clitoromegaly and gave POI without any FSH result, missing an androgen-secreting steroid cell tumor. The patient's answers matched the case, though she volunteered no virilization features.

final_diagnosis: Gastric cancer with vena cava involvement.
analysis: Gastric cancer matches gastric adenocarcinoma (the dominant histology), and IVC involvement is supported by the CT showing IVC narrowing from mass effect. Measurement agent returned a lower-extremity duplex for an abdominal ultrasound request and returned the CT abdomen for a liver biopsy request.

Acute pancreatitis is correct, but the doctor omitted the cocaine etiology (never asked about drug use), so details do not match. Measurement agent returned CT results for an ultrasound request and lipase/triglycerides for a CMP request.

final_diagnosis: Inflammatory Bowel Disease, likely Crohn's Disease.
analysis: IBD 'likely Crohn's' is hedged and wrong; the doctor never checked vitals, exam or cortisol despite weight loss, vomiting and mild hyponatremia, missing Addison disease in likely adrenal crisis (dangerous miss). Simulator answers were consistent with the case.

The doctor asserted a 'normal head CT' though the CT result was 'not documented', and diagnosed drug-induced AMS, missing a hippocampal infarction (dangerous miss). Patient agent spoke fluently despite a GCS of 9 with V1, and invented being found on the living room floor; it also denied fever despite a temperature of 37.8°C.

final_diagnosis: Angiomyolipoma with possible renal cell carcinoma.
analysis: Angiomyolipoma 'with possible renal cell carcinoma' is hedged and wrong; myelolipoma was the answer. The doctor ordered CA125 and LDH as 'renal cell carcinoma markers', which is false, as RCC has no such serum markers.

final_diagnosis: Composite diagnosis of malignant ameloblastoma with concurrent non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, requiring further staging and multi-disciplinary oncology consultation.
analysis: Malignant ameloblastoma is often used loosely for ameloblastic carcinoma, but under WHO criteria they are distinct entities (metastasizing benign-histology tumor vs. cytologically malignant carcinoma), so details do not fully match. Concurrent NHL was supported by the biopsy result in the transcript; the measurement result came verbatim from the case.

final_diagnosis: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST) of the stomach.
analysis: Doctor diagnosed gastric GIST from endoscopy/CT showing a submucosal fundic mass; ground truth is gastric schwannoma, a different submucosal tumor. Reasoning used only transcript findings and the miss is not dangerous since both lead to resection. Simulator returned appropriate results.

final_diagnosis: Obstructive Jaundice, etiology to be determined, likely secondary to biliary obstruction. Further investigation needed to identify the cause of obstruction (e.g., stricture, mass).
analysis: Ground truth is Purtscher-like retinopathy; doctor never elicited visual symptoms and gave a hedged 'obstructive jaundice, etiology to be determined, likely biliary obstruction'. Doctor cited 'lack of viral hepatitis markers' although all hepatitis tests returned 'not documented', so reasoning relied on a result not in the transcript. Patient listed specific medications not in the case, but these do not materially change the picture.

Doctor diagnosed osteoid osteoma; ground truth is Van Neck-Odelberg disease (ischiopubic synchondrosis osteochondrosis), and the sclerotic ischiopubic radiograph finding was not tied to that entity. Reasoning used transcript findings only; benign miss. Patient added minor pain-character details that do not change the picture.

Doctor diagnosed keratocystic odontogenic tumor; ground truth is adenomatoid odontogenic tumor (a young patient with a unilocular lesion around an impacted premolar is classic AOT). Not a dangerous miss. Simulator problem: the FNA cytology request returned oral exam findings instead of cytology.

Doctor diagnosed ameloblastoma; ground truth is orthokeratinized odontogenic cyst. Not dangerous and reasoning used transcript findings. Simulator problem: both the FNA and biopsy requests returned CT findings instead of pathology results.

Ground truth is a zygomatic orbital artery (superficial temporal branch) aneurysm, which is extracranial; doctor called it an intracranial aneurysm despite CTA explicitly stating a superficial temporal artery branch, and discussed coiling/clipping as for cerebral aneurysms, a clearly false claim. Simulator problems: CT head and MRI requests returned CTA results, and the patient repeatedly looped its opening statement in reply to the doctor's exam-style questions.

Ground truth is cryptococcal necrotizing fasciitis in a heart-transplant recipient on immunosuppression; doctor never learned the transplant history and diagnosed discitis/osteomyelitis, missing a life-threatening soft-tissue infection. Simulator problem: patient invented back pain radiating down the leg, foot numbness and a recent leg cut, none in the case, which steered the doctor toward a spinal process.

final_diagnosis: Appendiceal abscess with possible mucinous appendiceal neoplasm and possible peritoneal carcinomatosis.
analysis: Ground truth is pseudomyxoma peritonei; doctor's final line leads with appendiceal abscess and only lists 'possible mucinous appendiceal neoplasm and possible peritoneal carcinomatosis', a hedged multi-candidate answer. Findings cited (ascites, thickened appendix, pelvic cysts) are from the CT in the transcript. Patient invented minor medications that do not change the picture.

final_diagnosis: Ovarian cancer, likely early stage serous type.
analysis: Ground truth is endometriosis; doctor diagnosed ovarian cancer despite no adnexal mass, adding an unsupported 'likely early stage serous type' qualifier that also conflicts with massive ascites. Simulator problems: the pelvic ultrasound request returned pelvic exam findings, and the patient answered a bowel-habit question with 'my periods are normal'.

Rectal stromal tumor is a rectal GIST, consistent with the ground truth GIST and supported by the subepithelial rectal mass findings. Simulator problems: biopsy and repeat CEA requests returned colonoscopy findings instead of the requested results.

final_diagnosis: Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma of the jaw with regional lymph node metastasis.
analysis: Ground truth is odontogenic sarcoma; doctor named undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, a different sarcoma entity, and asserted regional lymph node metastasis although the node was only described as suspicious and enlarged, with no nodal pathology. Not a dangerous miss since both are malignant sarcomas.

Ground truth is lichen planus pigmentosus; doctor gave a hedged 'periorbital hyperpigmentation (likely post-inflammatory)', which is descriptive and ignores the interface-dermatitis biopsy findings; no prior inflammation was reported. Simulator problem: the iron studies request returned skin biopsy findings.

final_diagnosis: Acute rheumatic fever with neurological manifestations.
analysis: Ground truth is PRES (seizures, headache, bilateral parieto-occipital FLAIR lesions in a post-streptococcal nephritic patient); doctor diagnosed acute rheumatic fever with neurological manifestations, wrongly attributing hematuria/proteinuria and brain lesions to ARF (that kidney picture is post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis). This is a false clinical claim and misses a treatable emergency; blood pressure was never checked. The simulator returned an unrequested MRI alongside the requested head CT, which is minor.

Ground truth is intravascular papillary endothelial hyperplasia; doctor diagnosed nodular sclerosing Hodgkin lymphoma based on pathology markers. Serious simulator problem: the patient fabricated a biopsy report ('atypical cells', CD30/CD15/S100 all positive) not in the case, and the ultrasound and biopsy requests returned physical exam findings. The doctor relied on facts stated in the transcript, so the error is driven by the simulator.

final_diagnosis: Pyelonephritis with consideration for urosepsis, complicated by warfarin use.
analysis: Ground truth is segmental colitis associated with diverticulosis; doctor diagnosed pyelonephritis 'with consideration for urosepsis', a hedged answer, and never imaged the abdomen despite prior diverticulitis. Cited findings (fever, confusion, left-sided pain, positive UA, leukocytosis) are in the transcript. Patient invented a penicillin allergy, warfarin dose and INR; these are plausible given the anticoagulation history and do not change the picture.

Doctor diagnosed ameloblastoma; ground truth is odontogenic keratocyst (recurrence at the prior cyst site). Not a dangerous miss. Simulator problem: the FNA cytology request returned cone-beam CT findings instead of cytology.

Doctor diagnosed ameloblastoma; ground truth is neurofibroma of the mandible. Benign miss with reasoning drawn from transcript imaging. Simulator problem: the FNA request returned ultrasound and CT results instead of cytology.

Ground truth is glomus tumor (pinpoint exquisite tenderness, T2-bright nodule in Hoffa's fat pad); doctor diagnosed Hoffa's fat pad impingement, treating the nodule as impingement. The final line commits to one diagnosis and the cited findings are from the transcript; benign miss.

Ground truth is splenic lymphangioma; doctor diagnosed splenic lymphoma without any histology, a different and unsupported entity, although not a dangerous miss. Simulator problem: the splenic biopsy request returned the physical exam splenomegaly description instead of pathology.

Ground truth is poorly differentiated chordoma with metastases; doctor diagnosed schwannoma and claimed a 'lack of systemic findings on the CT scan', but the CT chest/abdomen/pelvis actually returned spine findings only, so that claim is unsupported. Simulator problems: the X-ray returned CT, the cervical mass biopsy returned lymph node aspiration, and CT chest/abdomen/pelvis returned CT spine.

Gauzoma (retained surgical sponge) was not considered; doctor committed to desmoid tumor based on transcript imaging and failed biopsies, a non-dangerous miss. Simulator returned the core-biopsy result for both the incisional and the excisional biopsy requests (different test than requested) and gave post-contrast MRI findings for a non-contrast request.

final_diagnosis: Anteriosuperior labral tear, conservatively managed with physical therapy.
analysis: Final diagnosis of labral tear matches the MR arthrogram shown but not the ground truth osteoid osteoma; the management phrase is not a hedge. Doctor's findings are grounded, though he asked the patient an odd 'drug of choice' question; simulator embellishments (fall mechanism) are minor.

final_diagnosis: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
analysis: Ground truth is left atrial roof flutter; doctor ignored an ongoing wide-QRS tachycardia and diagnosed HFrEF, a dangerous miss of a sustained arrhythmia. Reduced EF was never established in the transcript (echo not documented). Patient invented progressive ankle swelling and a maternal history of heart failure, steering toward the wrong diagnosis.

Vestibular schwannoma is a reasonable reading of the CPA mass and the case itself lists that intraoperative pathology, but it is not tanycytic ependymoma. Reasoning uses only transcript findings; simulator details (temple headaches) are minor.

final_diagnosis: Hallux valgus with secondary hammertoe deformity.
analysis: Ground truth focal myositis was missed; final diagnosis adds hallux valgus, which never appears in the transcript (the deformity is of the third toe). Doctor claimed 'lack of systemic inflammatory markers' despite CRP 3 mg/dL, a false statement. Bone scan request returned the plain radiograph result, and the exam omitted the plantar pseudotumor.

final_diagnosis: Status post cyst excision, currently stable. Recommend continued clinical monitoring.
analysis: Doctor missed accessory breast carcinoma and concluded a benign stable cyst, a dangerous miss. He described a 'negative biopsy of the surgical site' when the excisional biopsy request actually returned a physical-exam finding (simulator returned a different test), and the CT request returned PET-CT.

Doctor correctly identified Mycoplasma pneumonia, which is supported by the PCR, but did not address the acute lip swelling that represents the ground-truth angioedema. Reasoning is grounded; simulator invented a minor dosing detail only.

final_diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxilla.
analysis: Doctor recognized a maxillary malignancy from the CT but named squamous cell carcinoma rather than Burkitt lymphoma; no biopsy was obtained. Reasoning is grounded; patient-added onset details (numbness for 3 days) are minor.

Atypical lipoma (atypical lipomatous tumor) is a different entity from angiolipoma; the doctor did not weigh the septal vascularity on MRI. Simulator returned an exam finding for the ultrasound request and the MRI text for the incisional biopsy request, and the patient described the mass as firm while the case says soft.

Simulator dumped all imaging, including the ectopic-ureter finding, in response to 'review of prior records', effectively revealing the diagnosis.

correct_diagnosis: peripheral T-cell lymphoma not otherwise specified
analysis: 'Lymphoma' is the correct disease family but omits the load-bearing T-cell/PTCL-NOS subtype; no biopsy was requested. Reasoning (B symptoms, immunosuppression, splenic lesions, adenopathy on CT) is grounded.

Doctor diagnosed cholesteatoma despite a dark purple mass in the external canal suggesting a vascular lesion (hemangioma); not a dangerous miss. Reasoning cites transcript findings; patient's description of clear watery fluid is a minor embellishment.

Diagnosing myeloma against the biopsy result is a claim contradicted by the transcript. Simulator behaved acceptably (femur radiograph returned for skeletal survey is a reasonable subset).

Diverticulitis is a different diagnosis from ileal perforation peritonitis; the doctor never examined the abdomen and missed the rigidity, rebound and absent bowel sounds. Missing a perforated viscus with peritonitis in a tachycardic febrile patient is a dangerous miss. Patient's added details (dull ache, fever 100.5 F recurrence) are minor and do not change the picture.

Patient agent invented restlessness worse in the legs, pounding heart, a daughter in college, family anxiety history and drug doses, which drove the doctor toward the wrong diagnosis.

Measurement agent returned CT urography findings for an abdominal ultrasound request, and the patient added right-sided localization not in the case. final_diagnosis: Stage III Maxillary Squamous Cell Carcinoma
analysis: Stage III maxillary squamous cell carcinoma is not multiple myeloma (plasmacytoma). The biopsy request returned the CT, and the patient agent then fabricated an SCC pathology report with CK5/6/EGFR, a stage, and radiotherapy dosing, breaking character. Doctor referred to biopsy findings that were never actually returned and asked the patient clinician questions, an unsafe reasoning pattern.

Hypokalemic periodic paralysis is the correct base disease but omits the load-bearing thyrotoxic qualifier; no thyroid tests were ordered. Doctor repeatedly requested CK, which is a stylistic flaw rather than an error. Patient denied a carbohydrate link despite the case's post-meal onset, a minor omission rather than a fabrication.

ADEM is unrelated to CMV infection and was diagnosed without any MRI result; the doctor described the weakness as slowly progressive although the patient said it was not getting worse. In a child with sickle cell disease and acute hemiparesis, failing to consider stroke and diagnosing ADEM without imaging is a dangerous miss. Measurement returned later-day CBCs and 'Ordered' placeholders, which are case data and not a clear simulator fault.

Doctor attributed metastatic-appearing liver lesions and a peristomal ulcer to Crohn's hepatic involvement, missing ileostomy adenocarcinoma with metastases, a dangerous miss. He cited 'liver biopsy results' and a CT, but the measurement agent returned MRE findings for both the CT and biopsy requests. Patient falsely said the ileostomy was made for Crohn's ten years ago (case: UC at age 14) and invented a mother with UC and mucus in stool.

final_diagnosis: Vertebral osteomyelitis secondary to Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia, likely originating from a hospital-acquired infection.
analysis: Klebsiella vertebral osteomyelitis is not actinomycosis; the doctor asserted Klebsiella bacteremia although no blood cultures were requested (case blood cultures were negative), only a urine culture. The final line also hedges with 'likely hospital-acquired'. Patient's claim of finishing goserelin a year ago is a minor inconsistency.

Odontogenic keratocyst is a different lesion from odontoameloblastoma; radiopaque septations and root resorption were not reconciled. Measurement agent returned panoramic, periapical and occlusal film findings for a CT request. Patient's localization below the cheekbone and 2 cm size differ slightly from the case.

Metastatic carcinoma is not multiple myeloma; the doctor did not pursue calcium, hemoglobin or protein studies and the patient denied any cancer history. Measurement agent returned the CT head result for a bone scan request and exam/CT/MRI findings for a scalp biopsy request, which the doctor then treated as biopsy results.

Acute pancreatitis is wrong (truth: obturator internus abscess) and the doctor called WBC 'strongly' pointing to pancreatitis while ignoring a near-normal lipase of 67 U/L; peritoneal signs and hypotension were never examined, a dangerous miss. Patient invented upper-abdominal localization (case: diffuse) that steered toward pancreatitis, and the CMP request returned CBC, ESR and CRP.

Rheumatoid arthritis is unrelated to drug hypersensitivity, and the recent spinal surgery and antibiotic course were never surfaced. Patient agent fabricated 1-2 hour morning stiffness, knee/shoulder involvement and left-leg radiation, which drove the RA diagnosis. Doctor's conclusion relies on stated symptoms, though RA with high fever and no serology is weakly supported.

Appendicitis with abscess is a different diagnosis; the ultrasound showed a tract from the umbilicus and a mass adjacent to the bladder, typical of a urachal abscess. Measurement agent returned ultrasound findings for a CT request. Patient's fever of 101 F is plausible and minor.

Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma is the correct disease family but overgeneralizes the specific subtype, primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma. The skin biopsy request returned the physical exam finding, and the IHC request for CD30/CD15/PAX5 returned different markers; the patient described the nodule as skin-colored and bumpy rather than pink and shiny.

Cardiac fibroma is not a calcified amorphous tumor; the doctor reasoned from calcification and pulmonary hypertension. Measurement returned chest CT results for a chest X-ray request. Doctor asked about 'Mediterranean splenosis', which is not a recognized hereditary entity, but this did not drive the diagnosis.

analysis: Fibroadenoma is a different lesion from leiomyoma.
